DATED: 21/06/2023  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION NO. 2918 of 2023 ==========================================================
 SHAILESHKUMAR MAHOTJI SOLANKI  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT ==========================================================
Appearance:
CHINTAN U PATEL(7879) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR. KARAN U VYAS(6992) for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MS. KRINA CALLA, ADDL. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s)
No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE NIRZAR S. DESAI  Date : 21/06/2023  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By way of the present application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicant - accused has prayed for anticipatory bail in connection with the FIR being C. R. No.
11191035230003 of 2023 registered with Naroda Police Station, Dist. Ahmedabad for the offences punishable under Sections 376 and 506 (2) of the Indian Penal Code.
2. Learned advocate for the applicant submits that the nature of allegations are such for which custodial interrogation at this stage is not R/CR.MA/2918/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 necessary.
He further submits that the applicant will keep himself available during the course of investigation, trial also and will not flee from justice.

3. Learned advocate for the applicant on instructions states that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions including imposition of conditions with regard to powers of Investigating Agency to file an application before the competent Court for his remand.

He further submit that Shaileshkumar Mahotji Solanki vs State Of Gujarat on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183726309/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: upon filing of such application by the Investigating Agency, the right of applicant accused to oppose such application on merits may be kept open.
Learned advocate, therefore, submitted that considering the above facts, the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.

4. Learned advocate Mr. Kunal Patel appearing for the respondent - original complainant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State have opposed grant of R/CR.MA/2918/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 anticipatory bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.

5. Having heard the learned advocates for the parties and perusing the material placed on record and taking into consideration the facts of the case, nature of allegations, gravity of offences, role attributed to the accused, without discussing the evidence in detail, at this stage, I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.

6. This Court has considered the following aspects:-
(i) As per the FIR itself the complainant has stated that her husband borrowed a sum of Rs. 2,50,000/- before about one and half year before the incident and towards the repayment of the aforesaid amount, the cheque also was given to the present accused.
(ii) As per the FIR, the incident occurred on 24.12.2022 at around 2:30 p.m..

However, thereafter, the complainant had given an application before Naroda Police Station on R/CR.MA/2918/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 30.12.2022 stating that pursuant to the aforesaid amount borrowed by her husband on 20.12.2022 the present applicant came to her residence, demanded the money and quarreled with them.

Though he was given a cheque as the amount borrowed could not be managed to be repaid, the amount was not repaid and therefore, she has come to file a complaint against Shaileshkumar Mahotji Solanki but thereafter, compromise had arrived at between herself and the present applicant and therefore, she did not file any complaint stating that the present applicant has not misbehaved with her.

Though the aforesaid statement dated 30.12.2022 specifically states about the presence of the present applicant in her residence, she has not said anything about alleged offence by way of complaint before the concerned police station whereas in the FIR which was registered on 01.01.2023 has specifically stated that she informed about her husband R/CR.MA/2918/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 just before two days about the incident and therefore, FIR was registered on 01.01.2023 which would indicate that she informed her husband about the incident on 30.12.2022 and though she had gone to the concerned police station 30.12.2022, she did not got any FIR registered in respect of this offence which prima facie, indicates that the root behind the registration of FIR was the amount borrowed and despite the incident allegedly had taken place on 24.12.2022, the FIR was registered after delay of eight days.
(iii) There is no past antecedent registered against the present applicant.

sentences.text: (iv) The applicant is ready and willing to cooperate with the investigation.

(v) The present applicant is enjoying relief since 28.02.2023 and during this period till today, there is nothing on record to indicate that either he has tried to influence the witnesses or that he is not cooperating with R/CR.MA/2918/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 the investigation.
7. In the facts and circumstances of the present case, since the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required, I am inclined to consider the case of the applicant.

8. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors., reported at [2011] 1 SCC 694, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court reiterated the law laid down by the Constitution Bench in the case of Shri Gurubaksh Singh Sibbia & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab, reported at (1980) 2 SCC 565.
9.

sentences.text: (g) it would be open to the Investigating Officer to file an application for remand if he considers it proper and just and the learned Magistrate would decide it on merits;
10. Despite this order, it would be open for the Investigating Agency to apply to the competent Magistrate, for police remand of the applicant.

The applicant shall remain present before the learned Magistrate on the first date of hearing of such application and on all subsequent occasions,
as may be directed by the learned Magistrate.
This would be sufficient to treat the accused in the judicial custody for the purpose of entertaining application of the prosecution for police remand.

This is, however, without prejudice to the right of the accused to seek stay against an order of remand, if, ultimately, granted, and the power of the learned Magistrate to consider such a request in accordance with law.

It is clarified that the applicant, even if, remanded to the police custody, upon completion of such period of police remand, shall be set free immediately, subject to other conditions of this anticipatory bail order.
11. At the trial, the concerned trial court shall not be influenced by the prima facie observations made by this Court in the present order.
12. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
